verses.text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the 12 tribes which are scattered abroad: greeting.
My brothers and sisters, count it all joy when you fall into different temptations (tests).
Know this: the trying (testing) of your faith works patience.
But let patience have her perfect work, so that you may be perfect (complete) and entire, wanting (lacking) nothing.
If any of you lacks wisdom, let them ask of God, who gives to all men liberally (freely), and upbraids (scolds) not. And it will be given to them.
But let them ask in faith, not wavering (doubting) at all. For the one who wavers (doubts) is like a wave of the sea, driven with the wind and tossed.
For let not that man think that he will receive anything from the Lord.
A double minded man (one who cannot decide) is unstable in all his ways.
Let the brother of low degree (who is poor) rejoice in that he is exalted (lifted up).
But let the rich man rejoice in that he is made low. For as the flower of the grass he will pass away.

For the sun has no sooner risen with a burning heat, than it withers the grass. And the flower of the grass falls, and the grace (beauty) of its look perishes. So also the rich man will fade away in his ways.
Blessed is the man who endures temptation (testing). For when he is tried (tested), he will receive the crown of life, which the Lord has promised to those who love Him.
Let no man say when he is tempted: I am tempted by God. For God cannot be tempted with evil, and God does not tempt any man.
But every man is tempted when he is drawn away by his own lust (wrong desire), and enticed (pulled in).
Then when lust (wrong desire) has conceived, it brings forth sin. And sin, when it is finished, brings forth death.
Do not err (be fooled), my beloved (dear) brothers and sisters.
Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above. It comes down from the Father of lights. With Him there is no variableness (changing), neither shadow of turning.
Of His own will God begat (gave new birth to) us with the word of truth, so that we should be a kind of firstfruits (first part) of His creatures.
So, my beloved (dear) brothers and sisters, let every person be swift (quick) to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath (anger).
For the wrath (anger) of man does not work the righteousness (what is right) of God.
So lay apart all filthiness (dirt) and superfluity of naughtiness (overflowing evil). And receive with meekness (gentleness) the engrafted (planted) word, which is able to save your souls.
But be doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving (fooling) your own selves.
For if anyone is a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like a man looking at his natural face in a glass (mirror).
For he looks at himself, and goes his way, and right away forgets what kind of man he was.
But whoever looks into the perfect law of liberty (freedom), and continues in it, not being a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man will be blessed in his deed.
If any man among you seems to be religious, and does not bridle (control) his tongue, but deceives (fools) his own heart, this man's religion is vain (empty).
Pure religion and undefiled (clean) before God and the Father is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction (trouble), and to keep oneself unspotted (clean) from the world.

1.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses.

verses.text: My brothers and sisters, do not have the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons (treating some people better than others).
For suppose a man comes into your assembly (meeting) with a gold ring, in goodly (fine) clothes. And there comes in also a poor man in vile (dirty) clothes.
And you have respect to (honor) the one who wears the gay (fancy) clothing, and say to him: Sit here in a good place. And you say to the poor man: Stand there, or sit here under my footstool.
Are you not then partial (unfair) among yourselves? Have you not become judges with evil thoughts?
Hearken (listen), my beloved (dear) brothers and sisters. Has not God chosen the poor of this world, rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which He has promised to those who love Him?
But you have despised (looked down on) the poor. Do not rich men oppress (crush) you, and drag you before the judgment seats?
Do not they blaspheme (speak against) that worthy name by which you are called?
If you fulfil the royal law according to the Scripture, You shall love your neighbor as yourself, you do well.
But if you have respect of persons (treat some people better than others), you commit sin. And you are convinced (shown guilty) by the law as transgressors (lawbreakers).
For whoever keeps the whole law, and yet offends (fails) in one point, is guilty of all.
For the One who said, Do not commit adultery, also said, Do not kill. Now if you commit no adultery, yet if you kill, you have become a transgressor (lawbreaker) of the law.
So speak, and so do, as those who will be judged by the law of liberty (freedom).
For the one who has showed no mercy will have judgment without mercy. And mercy rejoices against (wins over) judgment.
What does it profit (help), my brothers and sisters, if a man says he has faith, and does not have works? Can faith save him?
If a brother or sister is naked (without enough clothes), and destitute (without) of daily food,
And one of you says to them: Depart in peace, be warmed and filled. But you do not give them the things which are needful (needed) for the body. What does it profit (help)?
Even so faith, if it does not have works, is dead, being alone.
Yes, a man may say: You have faith, and I have works. Show me your faith without your works, and I will show you my faith by my works.
You believe that there is one God. You do well. The devils also believe, and tremble.
But will you know, O vain (empty) man, that faith without works is dead?
Was not Abraham our father justified (shown to be right) by works, when he had offered Isaac his son on the altar?
Do you see how faith worked with his works, and by works faith was made perfect (complete)?
And the Scripture was fulfilled which says: Abraham believed God, and it was imputed (counted) to him for righteousness (being right with God). And Abraham was called the Friend of God.
You see then how by works a man is justified (shown to be right), and not by faith only.
In the same way also, was not Rahab the harlot (prostitute) justified (shown to be right) by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way?
For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.

2.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. verses.text: My brothers and sisters, do not be many masters (teachers). For you know that we will receive the greater condemnation (judgment).
For in many things we all offend (fail). If any man does not offend (fail) in word, the same is a perfect (fully grown) man. He is able also to bridle (control) the whole body.
Look, we put bits in the horses' mouths, so that they may obey us. And we turn about their whole body.
Look also at the ships. Though they are so great, and are driven by fierce winds, yet they are turned about with a very small helm (steering board), wherever the governor (pilot) wants.
Even so the tongue is a little member (part), and boasts (brags) great things. Look how great a matter a little fire kindles (sets burning).

And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity (sin). So is the tongue among our members (parts), that it defiles (makes dirty) the whole body. It sets on fire the course of nature (the whole of life). And it is set on fire by hell.
For every kind of beasts, and of birds, and of serpents (snakes), and of things in the sea, is tamed, and has been tamed by mankind.
But no man can tame the tongue. It is an unruly (out of control) evil, full of deadly poison.
With it we bless God, even the Father. And with it we curse men, who are made after the similitude (likeness) of God.
Out of the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers and sisters, these things ought not to be so.
Does a fountain (spring) send out sweet water and bitter at the same place?
Can the fig tree, my brothers and sisters, bear olive berries? Or a vine, figs? So no fountain (spring) can give both salt water and fresh.
Who is a wise man and endued (filled) with knowledge among you? Let him show out of a good conversation (way of life) his works with meekness (gentleness) of wisdom.
But if you have bitter envying (jealousy) and strife (fighting) in your hearts, do not glory (brag), and do not lie against the truth.
This wisdom does not come down from above. But it is earthly, sensual (of the body), devilish.
For where envying (jealousy) and strife (fighting) are, there is confusion and every evil work.

But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be intreated (asked). It is full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality (being unfair), and without hypocrisy (pretending).
And the fruit of righteousness (what is right) is sown in peace by those who make peace.

verses.text: Where do wars and fightings among you come from? Do they not come from here, even from your lusts (wrong desires) that war in your members (body)?
You lust (strongly want), and do not have. You kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain (get). You fight and war, yet you do not have, because you do not ask.
You ask, and do not receive, because you ask amiss (wrongly), so that you may spend it on your lusts (wrong desires).

You adulterers and adulteresses (people unfaithful to God), do you not know that the friendship of the world is enmity (hate) with God? So whoever wants to be a friend of the world is the enemy of God.
Do you think that the Scripture says in vain (for nothing): The spirit that dwells (lives) in us lusts to envy (wants jealously)?
But God gives more grace. So He says: God resists (stands against) the proud, but gives grace to the humble.
So submit yourselves to God. Resist (stand against) the devil, and he will flee (run away) from you.
Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners. And purify (make pure) your hearts, you double minded (who cannot decide).
Be afflicted (sorry), and mourn, and weep. Let your laughter be turned to mourning, and your joy to heaviness (sadness).
Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and He will lift you up.

Do not speak evil of one another, brothers and sisters. The one who speaks evil of his brother, and judges his brother, speaks evil of the law, and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law, but a judge.
There is one lawgiver, who is able to save and to destroy. Who are you that judges another?
Come now, you who say: Today or tomorrow we will go into such a city, and stay there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain (make money).
But you do not know what will happen tomorrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour (mist), that appears for a little time, and then vanishes away.
Instead you ought to say: If the Lord wills, we will live, and do this, or that.
But now you rejoice in your boastings (bragging). All such rejoicing is evil.
So to the one who knows to do good, and does not do it, to that one it is sin.

5.source: Rewritten 2026-11-20 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences), at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. verses.text: Come now, you rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that will come on you.
Your riches are corrupted (rotted), and your clothes are motheaten.
Your gold and silver are cankered (rusted). And their rust will be a witness against you, and will eat your flesh as if it were fire. You have heaped (piled up) treasure together for the last days.

Look, the hire (pay) of the workers who have reaped (harvested) your fields, which you kept back by fraud (cheating), cries out. And the cries of those who have reaped (harvested) have entered into the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth (the Lord of all armies).
You have lived in pleasure on the earth, and been wanton (wild). You have nourished (fattened) your hearts, as in a day of slaughter.
You have condemned (judged guilty) and killed the just (person who is right with God). And he does not resist (fight back against) you.

So be patient, brothers and sisters, until the coming of the Lord. Look, the husbandman (farmer) waits for the precious fruit of the earth. He has long patience for it, until he receives the early and latter rain.
You also be patient. Stablish (make strong) your hearts. For the coming of the Lord draws near.
Do not grudge (complain) against one another, brothers and sisters, so that you are not condemned (judged guilty). Look, the Judge stands before the door.
Take, my brothers and sisters, the prophets, who have spoken in the name of the Lord, for an example of suffering affliction (trouble), and of patience.

Look, we count them happy who endure. You have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord (what the Lord did in the end). You have seen that the Lord is very pitiful (full of pity), and of tender mercy.

But above all things, my brothers and sisters, do not swear, not by heaven, not by the earth, not by any other oath. But let your yes be yes, and your no, no, so that you do not fall into condemnation (being judged guilty).
Is anyone among you afflicted (suffering)? Let them pray. Is anyone merry (happy)? Let them sing psalms.
Is anyone sick among you? Let them call for the elders of the church. And let the elders pray over the sick person, anointing (rubbing) the sick person with oil in the name of the Lord.
And the prayer of faith will save the sick, and the Lord will raise the sick person up. And if the sick person has committed sins, they will be forgiven.

Confess (tell) your faults to one another, and pray for one another, so that you may be healed. The effectual (working) fervent (on fire) prayer of a righteous (right with God) man availeth (does) much.
Elijah was a man subject to like passions (feelings) as we are. And he prayed earnestly that it might not rain. And it did not rain on the earth for three years and six months.
And he prayed again, and the heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth her fruit.
Brothers and sisters, if any of you err (wander) from the truth, and one converts (turns back) that person,
Let him know that the one who converts (turns back) the sinner from the error (wrong) of his way will save a soul from death, and will hide a multitude (great number) of sins.
